.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r13/task/tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual}/judge.toml (judge header; keyword search of all criterion descriptions for stop / cross-criterion wording)
evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode = "batched" with aggregation = "weighted_mean" (42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual criteria) and each prompt carries explicit score-on-its-own and continue-after-failure wording. task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:10-11: "Never carry a verdict across criteria. Two similar criteria are two checks, and a failure in one must not fail another whose own steps passed." / "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session."; :15 "Fail fast: after two failed attempts at the same control or step, stop and fail that criterion, then continue with the rest." (the stop is scoped to one criterion, same as the frozen template). task/tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:10: "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session."; :11 "Attempt every criterion; one you could not attempt is failed and reported as such." task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:13: "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure or low score; return a score for every criterion. ... Give every criterion its own observation and never carry a score across criteria." Browser-tool errors are also scoped per criterion in all three ("retry once, then fail that criterion and move on"; visual: "give that criterion the lowest score you can justify ... and move on"). The only all-or-nothing rule in each scored prompt is the global browser gate ("If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension"), which is the template's own gate and is required by check 29, not a stop-on-first-failure instruction. A keyword search of the three prompts, app_context.md and every criterion description found no instruction to stop, skip or zero remaining criteria after a miss; app_context.md reinforces independence for the most likely shared failure: "Run may be broken in a submitted app. Criteria that do not depend on Run are still scored on their own steps; a criterion whose steps need a working Run fails if Run does not work." Cross-references in criteria ("scored elsewhere, not here") separate observables rather than inherit verdicts. Counterexample attempts: (a) app with broken Run - prompts do not let Run-dependent failures zero the editor/persistence criteria; (b) app failing the first functional criterion - the judge is told a failed criterion never ends the session. Neither produced a defect. Gate dimensions are exempt and were not assessed. Evidence limits: the index hashes I recomputed (results/runtime.json e47b63b0..., results/polish.json d65b6cf7..., hosted scored/reward-details.json bacbf94c...) match. The hosted run is on an earlier candidate and scored functional 41/41 and polish 6/6, so no run shows the judge actually continuing after a failed binary criterion; the visual dimension did return distinct per-criterion scores (1.0, 0.75, 1.0). The private check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed; this is a manual reading of the wording. No configured judge run exists for these bytes.
